newsitem.title: CANADA: Wascana CEO says company turnaround on track.
newsitem.headline: Wascana CEO says company turnaround on track.

text.p: Wascana Energy Inc, target of a C$1.7 billion takeover bid from Talisman Energy Inc, is reaping rewards from its turnaround stategy and expects to pump out more financial and production gains this year, Wascana chief executive Frank Proto said on Friday.

Proto, who would not speak specifically about Talisman's offer, told a conference call that he expected Wascana's oil production to average 65,000 barrels per day in 1997, up from 51,400 barrels per day in 1996.
Oil output was projected to reach 73,000 barrels per day by the end of the year, he said.
Natural gas production was expected to average 235 million cubic feet per day in 1997 and reach 260 million cubic feet per day by yearend, he said.
Wascana produced an average of 200 million cubic feet per day of gas in 1996.
Proto said the company was on track to meet its return on equity target of 10 percent this year. Wascana had a return on equity of over six percent in 1996 and 2.7 percent in 1995.
He said cash flow per share in 1997 was forecast at C$3.35 to C$3.55 and earnings per share at C$0.50 to C$0.55.

Proto cautioned, however, that commodity prices and Wascana's "successful efforts" method of accounting -- where exploration results show up immediately on a company's bottom line -- made earnings predictions difficult.
The company rang up earnings of C$0.43 per share and cash flow of C$2.61 per share in 1996.

Proto said a strong operational showing in 1996 and further gains expected this year showed that the firm's two-year-old turnaround plan, which included aggressive drilling and reserve replacement targets, was working.
"This really began in 1995, the first year that Wascana replaced its annual production through the drill bit and that momementum just continued to grow and build during 1996," Proto said.
"It shows that the plan we put in place is working. It shows that it's one of the well-executed plans and it's getting results for shareholders," he said.
Talisman said on February 12 it planned to offer C$18.50 in cash or 0.41 of a Talisman share for each share of Wascana, the Regina-based firm once owned by the Saskatchewan government.

Proto said he was unable to discuss the takeover situation -- including whether the firm would open a data room for prospective rival suitors -- until Wascana received and reviewed Talisman's formal bid document.
"To date, no offer has been received and our board of directors will be meeting after that offer has been received to make those kinds of decisions," he said.
Wascana shares on Friday were trading down 0.20 at 18.40 on the Toronto Stock Exchange. Talisman was down 0.40 at 44.35.
